thread:
Sam L: Quick async check — we need to lock a deprecation window for the unpinned-default change. Ops wants a clear signal to customers + an automated fast-follow allowance. Proposal: 10-week public notice, 4-week opt-in SDK migration period, then 2-week grace before hard flip. Thoughts?

Jess C: 10wk sounds fine. Are we also publishing a machine-readable calendar so partners can auto-update?

Sam L: Yeah thinking a calendar + an API endpoint /deprecation-status and an http header we can surface in proxied responses, e.g. `X-Redwood-Deprecation: model-default; date=2025-05-12; severity=warning`

Emily R: I like the header idea. Two quick asks: 1) define severity levels (notice, warning, critical) and 2) ensure header doesn't break clients that parse custom headers naively. Keep it ascii, short.

Liam T: +1. Also we should provide an `Accept-Model` negotiation hint: clients can send `Accept-Model: v1, v2;q=0.8` and we return `Accept-Model-Applied: v1` or `Accept-Model-Fallback: v2` so they can log/telemetry it. That helps debugging during rollout.

Maria P: For the SDKs: we should add an opt-in flag `autoFollowDefaultUnpin` that will automatically pick the new default during the SDK migration window. If enabled, SDK will emit telemetry events with `accept_model` and the `deprecation_header` values.

Sam L: Good. Ops also asked for a "fast-follow" safety valve: if we see >1% error/regression on evals tied to the change, auto-pause the flip and extend grace by 2 weeks. We'll need an eval hook name and a threshold param. Thoughts on naming? `regression_pause_threshold`?

Jess C: `regression_pause_threshold` is clear. Where do we run evals from — cloud infra or per-customer? If global, might be noisy. Suggest both: global signal + per-customer gated pause if that customer's traffic spikes errors.

Emily R: Agree. We should also document expected latency/throughput changes for the new default model and include a small sample of non-regression prompts used in canary checks. That prevents surprises when customers hit higher costs.

Liam T: One more edge-case: clients that pin by `model` field in body vs clients using header negotiation. We must define precedence: explicit body pin > `Accept-Model` > server default. Add failure code when body pin is incompatible with region/model availability, e.g. `422 model_unavailable` with `x-redwood-fallback` header listing applied fallback.

Maria P: For comms: marketing will need a short FAQ & countdown banner we can include in account console. Recommend we publish a timeline stub in the docs repo now and update as we firm dates.

Sam L: Actionable items I can volunteer to own: 1) write RFC for header semantics + precedence rules, 2) draft the deprecation-status endpoint schema, 3) coordinate SDK opt-in flag PR. Who can own regression hook + canary prompt set?

Emily R: I'll own the regression hook and canary prompt set. I'll post a short doc with the prompt corpus and thresholds by tomorrow.

Liam T: I'll prototype the `Accept-Model` negotiation headers and server response headers. Will open a small patch to router to surface fallback header.

Jess C: I'll start a docs stub and the FAQ draft. Will ping comms for banner copy.

deploy-bot: deployment queued — router/headers-proto -> staging (sha: b4c3d2a). Auto-tests: 42 passed, 1 flaky (telemetry).

Sam L: Thanks everyone. One final note: timeline anchor — propose we publish initial notice next Monday (3519992000 epoch-ish) and hold public flip ~10 weeks later. If anyone objects to those dates, speak now or DM me. :eyes: :thumbsup:
